findings.text: REQ-8 puts 'unchanged' in backticks, which makes it look like a glossary term or code identifier. It is neither.

rubric_items.reason: All five acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-8. The user-story motivation and any change to the dashboard tile are listed under Out of scope, each with a reason.
Most REQs are single and testable. REQ-2 sets its own window while REQ-4 says to reuse the tile's window, so the window rule is split across two REQs that could disagree.
Every known status cites a ticket line, a baseline section or an IDE answer (A-01..A-04). No values are invented, and nothing is marked assumed without a basis.
The undocumented dashboard 'Last 30 days' window and the missing glossary entry for 'Doctor page' were both raised as questions and answered by the user (A-01, A-04).
The questions offer real options with proposed defaults, ask only where the ticket was unclear, and all were answered in the IDE.
The wording is plain and glossary terms are used consistently. One small style issue: 'unchanged' is in backticks in REQ-8 as if it were a term.
